note: Uggeðla í tjörninni: the real recordings of the show's sound (remake/chapters/tjorn3d/sound.js, SLOTS). The show asks only for the files named under "files" here: a slot with no file plays the made sound named by its `instead`. The files are cut, shaped and levelled from Freesound HQ previews by `node remake/tools/tjorn3d-sounds.mjs`, which writes their entries: what each is in the show, its seconds and bytes, where it came from (title, author, page, preview, licence, the day it was fetched and the fingerprint of what was fetched), the fingerprint of the cut and what was done to it; `loop` is the stretch a looping file is played round ([from s, seconds]), and `level`, where a file has one, the gain it plays at instead of its slot's. All are CC0 1.0 (public domain): no credit is asked; it is given all the same in ../CREDITS.md. The owner said yes to fetching them on 2026-11-21 ("Já, sækja"); nobody had heard them when they were cut: the cuts are by measure. tests/tjorn3d-sound.test.mjs holds this file against the slots and the folder.

pond.what: the bed: a still pond, a loop of 20 s or more with no single call that would be known the second time round

rise.what: something big rising out of water, the water pouring off it: the rise begins at once and its fullest is about a second in

drips.what: drips falling back into still water, thinning: about 5 s

bubbles.what: a small burst of bubbles reaching the surface: 1 to 1.5 s, takes welcome

sink.what: something sinking softly, the water closing over it: its closing 0.6 s in

fish.what: a fish leaping out of the water: a light splash, under a second

frog.what: one croak of a frog, takes welcome

pond.mp3.what: the bed: the pond's still air and water, wind in the reeds far off; a loop

sources.title: Calm pond bright wind in reeds geese water TTP 190401.flac
sources.author: TRP

pond.mp3.done: An 84.8 s recording of a pond, stereo 48 kHz: an even wash of wind in reeds with small ticks of water, over a rumble, with geese calling at 46 to 50 s (far ones at 57 to 60 s and at 80 s) and gusts at 4 to 6, 19 to 25 and 41 to 44 s. Its two even stretches with no call and no gust, 60.45 to 80.35 s and 50.2 to 57.1 s, joined with a 1.2 s crossfade at equal power and the end passed into the start the same way: a loop of 24.4 s. 180 Hz high-pass (the rumble, which a tablet does not play), 6 dB off above 5 kHz (the reeds' hiss: 25 % of its energy lay over 6 kHz, now 12 %), 17 ticks more than 17 dB over the wash turned down to that (the most by 8.1 dB: a plop at 73.3 s that would be known the second time round), the left side was 2 dB louder than the right and they are made alike (they are all but unlike each other, correlation 0.38: it stays stereo), raised 23.2 dB to -24 dBFS RMS. 0.25 s of the loop's end is laid before it and 0.25 s of its start after it, and the show plays round from 0.25 s for 24.4 s, so that no decoder's padding falls in the round. MP3 128 kbps stereo 44.1 kHz with ffmpeg / libmp3lame. Now 24.9 s, its peak -7.5 dBFS after encoding.

rise.mp3.what: her head rises out of the water: a body lifting out of water, the water breaking and pouring off it, the first drips

sources.title: immersion in a bath and getting out of the bath.wav
sources.author: Zabuhailo

rise.mp3.done: Two recordings mixed. The body: a person getting out of a bath (18.4 s, mono 48 kHz; the heave measured at 9.93 s), from 9.05 to 13.4 s, played at 0.88 of its speed (slower and 2.2 semitones lower, for size), so the heave is 1 s in. The break: a head coming up out of water (10.8 s, the same on both sides; the surface breaks at 4.51 s), from 3.48 to 7.6 s at 0.92 of its speed, 4 dB under the body, its break 1.12 s in: the pouring peaks just after the surge. 150 Hz high-pass on both, 60 ms fade-in, the last 1.6 s faded out, the peaks shaved 5 dB by a limiter (a splash's one sample is not its loudness), the peak then at -3 dBFS. Its fullest 0.2 s is 1 s in; 0 % of its energy under 150 Hz, 7 % over 6 kHz (the body alone had 8 % over 6 kHz before it was slowed). MP3 96 kbps mono 44.1 kHz with ffmpeg / libmp3lame. Now 4.943 s, its peak -3.3 dBFS after encoding.
